blocks.text: Ozone is a powerful oxidising agent. It is non-toxic in small concentrations, but above 100 parts per million it is toxic; it harms humans and plants and attacks materials such as rubber, fabric dyes and the durability and appearance of paints.

blocks.prompt: Ozone protects us in the stratosphere but harms us at ground level. Explain the difference.
blocks.explanation: High in the stratosphere ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet light before it reaches the surface. At ground level it is a secondary pollutant made from NOx and VOCs in sunlight, and as a powerful oxidiser it damages lungs, plants, rubber, dyes and paint.

items: Ground-level ozone: strong oxidiser, toxic above 100 ppm; harms people, plants, rubber, dyes and paints.
